key_insight: Trigonal selenium appears intrinsically defect tolerant: even though point defects introduce deep levels, both nonradiative and radiative defect-assisted recombination are too weak to explain the observed photovoltaic losses.
engineering_relevance: This suggests t-Se is a promising wide-band-gap absorber for tandem and indoor photovoltaics, where defect tolerance can reduce performance penalties from realistic defect populations.
method: First-principles calculations of point defects in trigonal selenium
Shockley-Read-Hall recombination analysis for both radiative and nonradiative channels
Evaluation across a large, chemically diverse defect set under varying doping conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports large lattice reorganizations and energy releases of at least 0.5 Eg per recombination event, which strongly suppress nonradiative multiphonon emission and keep overall SRH rates too small to explain device losses.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on calculated defect scenarios, so real-device performance may still depend on defect concentrations, processing conditions, and other non-ideal loss mechanisms not captured here.
paper_title: Defect Tolerance in Trigonal Selenium Photovoltaics
